assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new door: a tunable platform in which flat moire bands produce correlated insulators and superconductivity, observed in transport and then confirmed by scanning-probe and spectroscopic imaging. The original experiment, with its clear and widely reproduced signatures, is the kind of discovery the prize is meant for, and it created a large field of moire quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction supplies the theoretical origin and the Jarillo-Herrero group's correlated-insulator and superconductivity measurements the original experimental discovery. This is a clean three-person configuration. The credited list omits the first author of the experimental papers (a junior researcher) and I recall that others made earlier related theoretical observations, so I would check the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across several platforms within a few years, and the basic interpretation (flat bands, correlation-driven states) is stable. The origin of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is secure. Timing is good given the rapid, well-documented impact.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unresolved, though the discovery does not depend on it.
Earlier theory and the role of junior experimentalists could complicate the credit; I have not independently verified the priority chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Practical correction of spherical aberration made sub-angstrom imaging and single-atom spectroscopy routine in TEM and STEM. It is an invention that changed what can be seen, with decades of verified impact on materials, catalysis, interfaces and quantum materials. Declared conflict: this is my own field, so I weigh it with care and apply the same standards of original instrument work as for any other candidate.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider and colleagues built the first working TEM corrector, and Krivanek and colleagues realized the STEM corrector. Other key contributors (for example Urban, Kabius, Dellby and Batson) are not in the supplied credit, which is a real problem because the three-person limit cuts across a collaborative effort.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Aberration-corrected instruments have been in wide use since the early 2000s, with resolution gains confirmed independently by many laboratories, and early recognition by other major prizes. Recognition is timely or even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Rose, Haider, Urban, Kabius, Krivanek, Dellby and Batson is contentious and I could not settle it from the supplied text.
Whether the committee views an instrument-technique advance as a physics invention of sufficient breadth relative to discovery-driven candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's proposal of the magic wavelength and realized at 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, are a major measurement invention. They open the door to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first lattice clock; Ye's group drove it to record precision and many applications. Others (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom) did essential work, but a two-person prize is defensible and based on the original idea and execution.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation from clocks at several national laboratories and cross-comparisons. The technique is stable and still improving. Timing is good, though redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Overlap with the optical-frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes already given may affect how the committee frames novelty.
Credit among Katori, Ye, Lemonde and others may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, with experimental verification in HgTe quantum wells and later in 3D materials by ARPES, defined a new class of matter and has strongly influenced materials research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theory, and Molenkamp's group did the original experimental demonstration of the quantum spin Hall state. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (the HgTe prediction; Zhang is deceased) and the 3D topological-insulator experiments (Hasan, Cava, Shen and others) are outside the supplied credit, so the configuration leaves out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by independent groups and now textbook physics, with heavy applications work still emerging. Recognition is somewhat overdue relative to the 2016 topological-phase prize.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize leaves enough unrecognized novelty.
Credit between the 2D and 3D experimental lines, and the missing HgTe theory, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductivity (LaFeAsO with F doping, 2008) was a surprise: a second family of high-Tc superconductors unrelated to cuprates, with a very rapid, widely reproduced follow-up. The original experiment is clear.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the original discovery at 26 K, which sets the priority. Chen and Zhao showed rapid Tc enhancement to above 40 K and 50 K in related compounds, which is important but a later improvement rather than the original discovery; I would suggest Hosono alone, with the committee deciding whether to add one of the others.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed for over 15 years, with a broad experimental base. The pairing mechanism is still unsettled, and Tc values remain below cuprates, which may weigh against.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism not understood and no application yet.
Whether the Chen and Zhao contributions count as a distinct discovery or an improvement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube detected high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 associations opened neutrino astronomy as an observational window. An instrument-driven discovery of a new kind of messenger.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Spiering led the Baikal and AMANDA-era neutrino telescope development and the IceCube collaboration's physics. The discovery is a large-collaboration result, and credit to the founders of neutrino telescopes (for example Markov, Learned, Roberts and Bahcall-related efforts) is not captured.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux well established, with source identification still limited to a few cases. Probably early for the source-level science but not for the discovery of astrophysical neutrinos.
uncertainties: Credit distribution in a very large collaboration with predecessors in DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA.
Source identifications are at modest significance, so interpretation could still change.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultra-pure hBN crystals are the substrate and encapsulant that enabled high-mobility graphene and the whole family of van der Waals heterostructures and moire physics. It is a materials and enabling tool of very large practical importance, appealing to someone who judges by what can be measured.
assessment.attribution: Watanabe and Taniguchi grew and supplied the crystals, which is a clean attribution to the original source. The difficulty is whether enabling materials growth counts as a physics discovery or invention in the prize sense.
assessment.maturity: Verified by use in hundreds of groups for a decade or more. Mature in impact. No competing source of equal quality.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards crystal growth as a prize-worthy invention rather than an enabling resource.
The specific discovery date and the precise growth contribution are not specified in the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction and observation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators achieved quantized Hall conductance without an external field, an experimentally clear result that is important to fundamental physics and low-dissipation electronics.
assessment.attribution: Dai and Fang (with collaborators) made the 2010 theoretical prediction in Cr/Fe-doped Bi2Se3 family materials, and Xue's group made the 2013 first observation. Haldane's earlier model and the Zhang group's role (Zhang deceased) and the work by others on better samples with higher quantization temperatures complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced independently, but quantization still occurs only at low temperatures, and the benefit to technology remains prospective. A little early relative to higher-ranked candidates.
uncertainties: Relationship to Haldane's 1988 model, already recognized in 2016, and to the topological-insulator candidate.
Low operating temperature limits practical impact for now.
